decode_concurrency_with_mtp_20260921.question: does the 2.5x aggregate from four streams (2026-09-18, speculation off) stack with MTP speculation, which already verifies 4 tokens per pass?
decode_concurrency_with_mtp_20260921.method: tools/decode_concurrency.py --n 128 on the production build (bin/hip-rocm101), server started by tools/manager.py with profile {parallel: 4, context: 65536} - everything else the default: MTP on with the shared-Q4_K_M-head-iq4_xs draft, draft_max 3, QSA on, vision on, 96 GB carve, dedicated memory (unified=False). Short prompts, so attention/KV cost is negligible and this is the ceiling. Per-stream figures are the server's predicted_per_token_ms; 'sum' adds the streams' rates, 'wall' is tokens over wall-clock including prompt processing.

1 stream after.note: no thermal drift after the four-stream burst

decode_concurrency_with_mtp_20260921.reading: 1.54x at four streams with MTP (37.5 -> 57.7) against 2.5x without it (19.0 -> 47.1). Both are the same lever - weight bytes read once per step shared by more tokens - and MTP had already taken most of it: a single stream verifies 4 tokens per pass, so four streams make a 16-token verify. A 4-token pass costs ~64 ms and a 16-token pass ~167 ms (69.4 ms/token x 2.4 accepted tokens per pass): 4x the tokens for 2.6x the time, which is close to bandwidth-linear because on a MoE the routed experts touched grow with the batch and only the trunk, attention and shared expert are read once.
decode_concurrency_with_mtp_20260921.load_limit: -np 4 fails to load at context 262144 (ROCm 'unspecified launch failure' at ~38 s, during the projector upload, i.e. a sticky error from the graph reserve; reproducible three times, also with unified memory, not memory pressure). Loads at 131072 and 65536. Bisected at 32768: MTP off, vision off, block-key cache off, decode gather off, QSA off and -np 2 all load, so the failure is the combination of four slots and the 262144 reserve, not one of the optimisations. DIAGNOSED (same day): HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 shows PAL 'failed to submit CMD' while the draft model loads. The mixed-sequence reserve (any parallel > 1) keeps a dense f16 KQ mask of n_ctx x ubatch, exactly 4 GiB at 262144 x 8192, which the driver will not fill: -np 2 fails the same way, -np 4 with ubatch 4096 (2 GiB) loads. But with the ubatch reduced to 7936 the first mixed prefill at 262144 still dies in a MUL_MAT ('unspecified launch failure' at the first four requests), while 131072 loads and serves four streams (12-14 tok/s each, 51 aggregate at 64 tokens). So the manager refuses parallel > 1 above 131072 (error multi_slot_context) rather than pretending.

decode_concurrency_8_slots_mtp_on_off_20.question: the expert-set model (512 experts, 10 per token, ~116 MB each: a batch of n tokens touches 512*(1-(502/512)^n) distinct experts) says the aggregate keeps rising with streams and that MTP's draft tokens compete with real users' tokens for the same expert bytes. Both testable at 8 slots.
decode_concurrency_8_slots_mtp_on_off_20.method: same as above with profile {parallel: 8, context: 65536} and mtp true / false; streams 1, 4, 8; 128 tokens each; the default server was restored afterwards.
decode_concurrency_8_slots_mtp_on_off_20.fit: speculation off: step = ~30 ms fixed + ~1.0 ms per distinct expert touched (116 MB at ~110-116 GB/s). Predicts 40 / 69 / 106 ms for 1 / 4 / 8 tokens against 39.9 / 66.6 / 112.1 measured. The 96 GB carve is why the single-token step is 40 ms here and was 50 ms on 2026-09-18 at 64 GB.
reading: MTP saturates at four streams: 62.4 sum at 4, 62.9 at 8. A 32-token verify is all expert bandwidth (238 distinct experts, ~27 GB per pass), so more streams only make each user slower (8 tok/s each).

MTP and concurrency compete for the same expert budget, and draft tokens are only 60-70% useful: at 8 streams MTP off wins, 71.4 against 62.9; at 4 they tie (60 vs 62); at 1 MTP wins by half (37 vs 25). The crossover is around four users.
Highest aggregate measured on this machine: 71.4 tok/s, 8 streams, speculation off, 8.9 tok/s per user - 2.85x the single-stream no-MTP rate, 1.9x the single-stream MTP rate.

The expert path streams at ~110 GB/s against ~210-220 achievable on this memory: at batch 8 each of the ~76 experts sees about one token, i.e. 76 x 3 small matrix-vector launches. That kernel-side gap, not bandwidth, is the remaining lever for concurrency, and it would help the single stream too.
decode_concurrency_8_slots_mtp_on_off_20.decision: default stays -np 1 with MTP on. For a multi-user deployment: 4 slots either way; beyond 4, MTP off. The multi-stream QSA work (mixed-sequence ubatches on the sparse decode path) is only worth doing for long-context multi-user use, and its ceiling is this ~1.5-1.9x.

expert_path_iq3s_mmq_20260921.question: where the expert kernels actually stand against the memory ceiling, and what of it is kernel rather than bytes
expert_path_iq3s_mmq_20260921.method: tests/test-backend-ops perf -o MUL_MAT_ID with STRIX_MOE_PERF (patch apply_iq3s_mmq_hip adds this model's shapes: 512 experts, 10 used, 640x2560 gate/up and 2560x640 down), GB/s = expected distinct experts touched (512*(1-(502/512)^n)) x expert bytes / time. n=1 and n=4 figures exceed DRAM bandwidth: the working set (7-36 MB) sits in the MALL between repetitions, so only n >= 8 is a DRAM number. In-situ check: STRIX_NODE_TIMING=1 GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 on real decode steps (tmp captures, not kept).
what_changed: IQ3_S MMQ tile loader on HIP: __vcmpne4/__vsub4 were byte loops (the mmvq vec-dot had already replaced them); sign bytes now come from two multiplies, +20% at 8-16 tokens
the IQ3_S grid is copied into LDS after the x tile: neutral within noise (the 2 KB table was L0-resident anyway), kept because it costs nothing

the fork's compact routed MoE MMQ path (mul_mat_q_routed_compact, RDNA3.5, 512 experts) was gated to IQ4_NL; opened to IQ3_S and IQ4_XS: the 24+ token cliff (73 GB/s) is gone, 156-173 GB/s to 64 tokens

decode_ab.method: tmp/decode_ab.py: production runtime against the build, same manager argv, 128 tokens per stream, short prompts, 96 GB carve

np1 mtp 1 stream.read: unchanged: a 4-token verify goes through mmvq, not MMQ

np4 mtp 4 streams.read: within the acceptance noise (prod's two runs differ by 15%)

np8 mtp 8 streams.read: +16%: the 32-token verify was on the cliff

expert_path_iq3s_mmq_20260921.reading: In the production configuration (one user, MTP, 4-7 tokens per verify) the expert kernels were already near the ceiling - the earlier '110 GB/s' came from attributing every per-token cost to the experts; the per-token costs that actually grow with the batch are the GDN state traffic (fp32 recurrent state, ~3 MB per sequence per layer, read and written every step), the PLE gather, and the per-token projections. What was kernel-bound was IQ3_S in MMQ (the multi-user regime) and the tiling cliff above 16 tokens; both are fixed. The remaining IQ3_S gap to IQ4_NL (157 vs ~190) is the format's unpacking, not memory.
not_done: GDN recurrent state in bf16 instead of fp32 would halve the per-sequence traffic that makes 8 streams cost 15 ms per step in GATED_DELTA_NET; numerics untested
tried_and_dropped: mmvq IQ3_S vec-dot with one dp4a per word (signed bytes by xor+add) instead of the two the sign split needs: 913/913 correct, no change at n=1/4/8 (295/332/150 GB/s-equivalent against 282-336 before). The cache-hot n<=4 figures already exceed DRAM bandwidth, so the single user's gate/up kernels are memory-bound as they stand; the 15% per-byte gap to IQ4_NL on a hot cache does not reach the wall clock. Reverted.
